question.text: If <math><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is a continuous function such that its value <math><mo>∀</mo><mi></mi><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>R</mi></math> is a rational number and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mn>1</mn></mfenced><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mn>2</mn></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, then the value of <math><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to

solution.text:
Since fx is continuous and attains only rational values, then by intermediate value theorem, fx is a constant function.

i.e. f1=f2=3
